elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: The line shows total external debt from 2015 to 2025. It rises overall from 4,671 to 7,724, with a marked increase around 2021 and some subsequent fluctuations.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 2
elements.title: External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations

data.label: Public & publicly guaranteed - by creditor type
Public & publicly guaranteed - by creditor type
Public & publicly guaranteed - by creditor type

elements.description: Connected stacked bars break down 2025 external debt first by debt category, then public and publicly guaranteed debt by creditor type, and finally multilateral and bilateral debt by creditor. Public and publicly guaranteed debt is the largest top-level component at 5,085, while private nonguaranteed debt is the smallest at 287. IMF-SDR allocations account for 4,213 of multilateral debt; among bilateral creditors, China is largest at 70 and other bilateral creditors are smallest at 28.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four small line charts show external debt and debt service relative to exports and GNI, alongside shaded percentile bands. The exports-based series run from 2015 to 2024, while the GNI-based series run from 2015 to 2025. The latest displayed ratio is highest for external debt / exports at 12% and lowest for debt service / GNI at 0.1%.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Note: Figure 3 shows no data values for the exports-based ratios after 2024. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two side-by-side boxes are labeled Official creditors and Private creditors. Each box lists Maturity, Grace period, and Interest rate, with '..' in place of every value. No values are shown because there were no new commitments in 2025.
elements.notes: Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for official or private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
